method.description: Commercial-permission determination on the Colorado Judicial Department JDF record-sealing form family. Three independent evidence channels were used: the issuer's own published statements about the JDF programme; the Colorado Judicial Branch's only located terms-of-use instrument; and first-hand measurement of the copyright notices actually printed on and embedded in the adopted Edition 1.2 assets for this family. The repository was searched for any retained written grant. No publisher was contacted, no binary was downloaded, no source was materialized, no receipt was written and no restricted form was reproduced.
method.issuerContactPolicy: This job must not contact the publisher. The assignment does not permit it, and a licence request is a business decision with an owner of record. Nothing here initiates or forecloses that decision.
method.restrictedFormsReproducedNote: No JDF form was excerpted, transcribed or embedded. The only form text reproduced anywhere in this record is footer identity strings and copyright-notice evidence, which is evidence about the work rather than the work.
method.byteVerificationNote: The twelve Colorado JDF record-sealing PDFs inspected here were materialized by an earlier authorized pass and each is covered by an existing source-materialization receipt. This job opened them read-only to read their copyright notices, page footers and XMP metadata. It materialized nothing, wrote no receipt and changed no file mode.

assignedQuestion.question: May LegalEase lawfully reproduce, redistribute, prefill, modify only the form fields of, and include in a paid self-help packet the exact Colorado Judicial Department forms assigned to this family — JDF 2370, JDF 2371 and JDF 2374?
assignedQuestion.answer: Not on any authority located. No instrument published by the Colorado Judicial Department or the Colorado Judicial Branch grants reproduction, redistribution, prefilled distribution or commercial use of these forms, and none places them in the public domain. The only Judicial Branch terms-of-use instrument located restricts its content to personal, non-commercial use and directs anyone whose use exceeds fair use to seek permission directly from the copyright holder. The family is therefore fail-closed pending a written grant.

ownership.owner: Colorado Judicial Department (the Colorado Judicial Branch), acting through the State Court Administrator's Office
ownerEvidence: The adopted Edition 1.2 asset for JDF 2374 carries PDF document Author and XMP dc:creator 'Colorado Judicial Department'. Read first-hand on 2026-08-07 from the materialized binary.
Sibling assets in the same family carry Author 'Colorado Judicial Department' or 'Colorado Courts'.

The issuer's own Judicial Department Forms (JDF) Administration page describes a five-phase forms programme in which changes are 'submitted to the Colorado Supreme Court for approval' before publication, and routes all form correspondence to Forms@judicial.state.co.us.
ownership.ownershipTransferredOrDedicatedNote: No dedication to the public domain, open licence, or transfer of rights was located in any Colorado Judicial Branch instrument.

governingTerms.assignedChannel: https://www.coloradojudicial.gov — the site that publishes JDF 2370, 2371 and 2374
governingTerms.assignedChannelFinding: The Colorado Judicial Branch publishes no terms of use, legal notice, copyright page or reuse policy on the site from which these forms are served. The archived home page and the archived Self-Help Forms index carry no such link; the only policy-type links in the footer are Accessibility Information and a Glossary of Legal Terms. The issuer's own JDF Administration page is silent on reuse: it covers form development, endorsement, Supreme Court approval, remediation and publication only.

nearestJudicialBranchInstrument.instrument: Terms of Use, Judicial Legal Help Center / Colorado Legal Help Center
nearestJudicialBranchInstrument.isAJudicialBranchPropertyEvidence: Its own limitation-of-liability clause binds 'THE COLORADO JUDICIAL BRANCH, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO ANY TRIAL COURT, ANY COURT OF APPEAL, THE SUPREME COURT, THE OFFICE OF THE STATE COURT ADMINISTRATOR, THE COLORADO LEGAL HELP CENTER ADVISORY BOARD, AND THEIR OFFICIALS, OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES, CONTRACTORS AND AGENTS'. Its security-contact address is library@judicial.state.co.us, on the Judicial Department's own domain.
nearestJudicialBranchInstrument.distributesJdfFormsEvidence: The site serves JDF form PDFs from its own document store, for example the JDF 402 civil protection order packet at lawhelp.colorado.gov/sites/lawhelp/files/documents/.
operativeTermsVerbatim: This Website and the Content are protected by applicable copyrights, and other proprietary and intellectual property rights. You do not acquire any ownership rights in the Content or this Website.

You may download publicly-available Content on this Website only for your personal, non-commercial use, provided that: (i) you keep intact all copyright and other proprietary notices; and (ii) if your copying or use of copyrighted materials on this Website is other than "fair use" under federal copyright laws, you must seek permission directly from the copyright holder.

You may not do any of the following: ... decompile, reverse engineer, disassemble, lease, sell, distribute, or reproduce this Website; ... remove or modify any copyright notices, other proprietary notices, or references to these Terms of Use in the Content or on this Website; or misrepresent the Content or this Website, or misinform others about the origin or ownership of the Content or this Website.
nearestJudicialBranchInstrument.scopeLimitOfThisInstrument: By its own words these Terms govern access to and use of that Website and its Content. They are not, on their face, the terms of coloradojudicial.gov. They are recorded here as the Judicial Branch's own expressed posture toward its self-help content, and as direct evidence that the Branch asserts copyright in that content and does not treat it as free for commercial reuse. They are not treated in this decision as a term binding on the coloradojudicial.gov publication of JDF 2370, 2371 and 2374.

copyrightNoticeMeasurement.corpus: All twelve Colorado JDF record-sealing PDFs materialized in this repository under existing source-materialization receipts.
copyrightNoticeMeasurement.method: Full text extraction with layout preservation, plus XMP packet inspection, plus a raw-byte and decompressed-stream scan for copyright strings.
copyrightNoticeMeasurement.result: None of the twelve carries a Colorado Judicial Department copyright notice. No '©', no 'Copyright' string and no XMP rights statement appears in any of them. Each page footer carries only the form number, the short form title, the revision line and the page number — for the assigned family, 'JDF 2374 - Order to Seal Conviction (conduct no longer prohibited)   R: July 1, 2025   Page 1 of 2'.

falsePositiveExcluded.observation: JDF 2374's raw bytes do contain the UTF-8 sequence for '©' twelve times and its decompressed streams contain copyright text.
falsePositiveExcluded.resolution: Every one of those is an embedded font-vendor notice — 'The Monotype Corporation. All Rights Reserved.' and 'Hebrew OpenType Layout logic copyright © 2003 & 2007, Ralph Hancock & John Hudson' — plus an MIT-style font permission notice. None is a Colorado Judicial Department copyright notice, and the twelve raw '©' byte hits fall inside compressed content streams, not in text. Recorded so that a later automated scan does not mistake a font licence for a document licence.

whyAbsenceIsNotPermission: Copyright notice has not been a condition of copyright in the United States since the Berne Convention Implementation Act took effect on 1 March 1989. An unmarked work published after that date is protected exactly as a marked one.

The Colorado Judicial Department demonstrably does assert copyright on part of the JDF series. Forms in other JDF sub-series carry the express notice '© <year> Colorado Judicial Department for use in the Courts of Colorado' — the JDF 402 civil protection order form served from the Branch's own legal-help site is a located example. So an unmarked JDF form is not evidence of a policy of non-assertion; it is evidence only about that form's footer.
The phrase the Department uses where it does mark a form — 'for use in the Courts of Colorado' — is a use limitation on its face, not a grant.
copyrightNoticeMeasurement.generalisationLimit: This measurement establishes the absence of a notice on these twelve documents only. It must not be restated as 'the JDF series carries no copyright notice', which is demonstrably false.

publicDomainAnalysis.federalGovernmentWorksRuleNote: 17 U.S.C. § 105 withholds copyright protection only from works of the United States Government, defined by 17 U.S.C. § 101 as works prepared by an officer or employee of the United States Government. It does not reach the works of a State or of a State's judicial branch. A Colorado Judicial Department form is not a federal government work.
publicDomainAnalysis.stateDedicationLocatedNote: No Colorado statute, Colorado Supreme Court rule, Chief Justice Directive or published policy placing JDF forms in the public domain or licensing them for reuse was located.

publicRecordsActArgumentRejected.argument: That a form published by a state agency is a public record and therefore freely reusable.
publicRecordsActArgumentRejected.why_rejected: Two independent reasons. First, the Colorado Open Records Act, C.R.S. § 24-72-201 et seq., governs the right of access to records; it does not confer downstream reproduction, adaptation or redistribution rights, and access is not a licence. Second, the Colorado judicial branch is not an 'agency' under CORA — access to court records is governed separately, under C.R.S. § 24-72-301 et seq. and the Judicial Branch's own public-access rules. Neither route reaches a commercial reuse permission.

edictOfGovernmentArgumentNotReached.argument: That a court-approved form is an 'edict of government' and so uncopyrightable, by analogy to statutes, judicial opinions and, after Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org (2020), annotations authored by a legislature's agent.
edictOfGovernmentArgumentNotReached.why: The doctrine turns on whether the author is a body vested with authority to make or interpret law acting in that capacity. A JDF form is approved by the Colorado Supreme Court but is a procedural convenience rather than an enactment or an interpretation, and no located Colorado authority addresses the question. Deciding it would be a legal opinion, which this lane does not issue.
edictOfGovernmentArgumentNotReached.consequence: It is named as the one substantive argument a licence owner might raise, so that the question is on the record rather than silently ignored. It is not relied on, and it must not be treated as a permission.

questionsResolved.question: Who owns the forms?
questionsResolved.answer: The Colorado Judicial Department, through the State Court Administrator's Office, with the Colorado Supreme Court approving form changes before publication.

questionsResolved.question: What terms govern reuse?
questionsResolved.answer: None are published for the channel that serves these forms. The Judicial Branch's only located terms-of-use instrument restricts its own site's content to personal, non-commercial use.

questionsResolved.question: Does the Judicial Branch authorize reproduction?
questionsResolved.answer: No authorization was located, express or implied.

questionsResolved.question: Does it authorize commercial reuse?
questionsResolved.answer: No. Nothing authorizes it, and the only Branch statement located excludes it for its own self-help content.

questionsResolved.question: Does it authorize prefilled distribution?
questionsResolved.answer: Not addressed anywhere. It is a second, separate permission that would still be unresolved even if reproduction were permitted, because prefilling produces a derivative rendering of the form bearing the Department's form number and revision.

questionsResolved.question: Are field-only modifications allowed?
questionsResolved.answer: Not addressed by the issuer. Note the distinction that matters: these are AcroForm PDFs designed to be completed, so a filer entering their own data into the fields is the intended use of the artifact. That says nothing about a vendor prefilling the same fields programmatically and selling the result, which is the act in question here.

questionsResolved.question: Is attribution required?
questionsResolved.answer: No attribution requirement is published for these forms. Where a JDF form does carry a copyright notice, the Branch's terms require that notices be kept intact and prohibit removing or modifying them. Independently, the JDF number and revision footer are the form's identity and must not be stripped, because doing so would misrepresent which revision a participant is filing.

questionsResolved.question: Are disclaimers required?
questionsResolved.answer: No issuer-imposed disclaimer was located. LegalEase's own non-attorney and no-legal-advice disclaimers are a separate product obligation and are outside this determination.

questionsResolved.question: Is written permission already available?
questionsResolved.answer: No. The repository retains no written grant, licence, correspondence or permission from the Colorado Judicial Department. The only licence-bearing decision in the corpus is the Kansas one, which is a different publisher and a different family.

questionsResolved.question: Does the result apply to both JDF-2370 and JDF-2371?
questionsResolved.answer: Yes, and to JDF 2374. All three are the same publisher, the same series, the same July 1 2025 revision and the same publication channel, and none carries a copyright notice or an accompanying term.

questionsResolved.question: Does the result apply to the broader JDF series?
questionsResolved.answer: The reasoning does; one factual finding does not. The absence of any published reuse term applies to the whole series because the Branch publishes none anywhere. The finding that no copyright notice appears on the form face is specific to the twelve record-sealing forms measured and must not be extended, because other JDF sub-series carry an express notice.

questionsResolved.question: Is the form limited to personal or noncommercial use?
questionsResolved.answer: For JDF content distributed through the Branch's legal-help site, expressly yes. For the coloradojudicial.gov publication of these three forms, the Branch has said nothing either way — which leaves the default position of copyright, not a permission.

prohibitedInferences: Public downloadability is not a licence. These forms are free, unauthenticated and openly served, and none of that grants reproduction, prefill or resale.
The absence of a © symbol is not a grant. Notice has not been required since 1989.
Government hosting does not create public domain. The federal-works rule in 17 U.S.C. § 105 does not reach state judicial branches.
Permission for a filer to complete and file a form is not permission for a vendor to prefill and sell it.
The Judicial Branch's silence on coloradojudicial.gov is not consent. Silence leaves the default, and the default is that the work is protected.
A prior automation block or a 403 response says nothing about permission and must not be conflated with a licence finding.

accessFactsObserved.note: Recorded as access facts only. They bear on retrieval, not on permission.

observations.note: A 403 here is not evidence that a terms-of-use page exists. The Wayback Machine holds no capture of this path at all, while it does hold captures of the home page, the Self-Help Forms index and the Forms Administration page — which is consistent with the path not existing.

archivedOfficialPagesRead.proves: the site footer offers no terms-of-use, legal-notice or copyright link

commercialEffect.allOfTheAboveBasis: Not prohibited by a located term — ungranted. Each act would use a presumptively copyrighted state judicial work without permission, and LegalEase has no permission.
whatRemainsPermittedAndUnaffected: Naming the forms, citing their numbers and revisions, and telling a participant which forms their situation requires.
Linking a participant to the issuer's own publication so that they obtain the official form from the court.
Guidance content LegalEase authors itself about how the process works.

Internal identity work: retaining the authority row, verifying bytes, and materializing the binary for verification. Materialization is an internal integrity act, not a distribution, and this determination neither authorizes nor forbids it; it blocks reproduction, prefill and sale in a participant-facing packet.

prohibitedWorkarounds: Do not relabel a JDF form as a LegalEase custom pleading. A retyped or reformatted copy of a Colorado Judicial Department form is a derivative of that form, not an original pleading, and the relabelling would also misrepresent the document's origin.

Do not strip the JDF number, title or revision footer to make a copy look unofficial. The Branch's own terms prohibit removing proprietary notices, and stripping the revision line would additionally leave a participant unable to tell which revision they are filing.
Do not substitute a commercial vendor's fillable derivative of a JDF form. A derivative carries the same underlying rights problem plus an unverified provenance.
Do not treat a successful download, before or after the current host block, as evidence of permission.
Do not proceed on the basis that no one has objected.

reopeningCondition.whatWouldReopen: Exactly one of the following, in writing and retained in the repository: (a) a written grant from the Colorado Judicial Department permitting reproduction, prefilled distribution and inclusion in a paid self-help packet, obtained through the Department's published forms channel Forms@judicial.state.co.us or through the State Court Administrator's Office; (b) publication by the Colorado Judicial Branch of terms of use or a reuse policy expressly permitting commercial reproduction and prefilled distribution of JDF forms; (c) a Colorado Supreme Court rule or Chief Justice Directive to the same effect; or (d) a reasoned legal determination by counsel of record, retained in the repository, that the forms are uncopyrightable edicts of government or that the intended use is fair use.
reopeningCondition.whoOwnsIt: The licence owner of record. This job is barred from contacting the publisher and made no contact.
reopeningCondition.whatWouldNotReopen: Another successful download; the passage of time; the absence of a copyright notice on a further JDF form; or a third party's practice of redistributing JDF forms commercially.

implementationFamilyRelationship.broaderFamilyExposure: The same determination governs every other Colorado track whose components bind a JDF form — co_clean_slate, co_motion_seal_conviction, co_motion_seal_nonconviction, co_multiple_conviction_seal, co_petition_seal_arrest, co_municipal_conviction_seal and co_pardoned_conviction_seal — because the publisher, the series and the absence of terms are identical. This job resolves the licence question for the assigned family; it does not restate the disposition on those other tracks' rows, which their own owners must carry.
implementationFamilyRelationship.familyReadinessStatement: No Colorado implementation family is ready and this job does not assert that any is. A negative licence result cannot make a family ready; it adds a distribution blocker on top of the identity, mapping and materialization blockers already recorded.

auth02Consequence.explanation: The JDF 2370 to JDF 2371 component remap is an accuracy correction and is independent of the licence outcome. It must proceed regardless: recording that JDF 2371 is the motion and JDF 2370 the guide is right whether or not LegalEase may ever reproduce either. If anything the remap matters more under a negative licence, because it determines which form LegalEase must tell a participant to obtain from the court.
auth02Consequence.memoEditedNote: CO.memo.json was not opened for writing and is not among this job's owned paths.
auth02Consequence.handoff: Session A creates or activates the AUTH-02 Colorado memo-correction child after this licence decision integrates, as the captain directed. This job neither creates it nor pre-empts its content.

materializationConsequence.explanation: Materialization is an internal verification act: it places issuer bytes where the factory can hash and inspect them. It is not a distribution to a participant and not a reproduction in a paid packet. This determination therefore does not itself bar the captain from materializing JDF 2371, which the identity decision recorded as materialization-required.
materializationConsequence.whatIsBlocked: Every participant-facing use: reproducing the form in a packet, prefilling it, rendering a filled copy, and selling any of that.
materializationConsequence.failClosedPosture: generationAllowed=false and licenseAdopted=false are recorded so the factory's own commercial-licence gate keeps this family from generating. Runtime stays disabled and packet_ready is unchanged.

amendmentHandoffItems.item: Licence disposition for the Colorado JDF form family
amendmentHandoffItems.detail: Edition 1.3 should carry an explicit licence disposition on these rows rather than leaving the commercial-use question unstated, so that a later reader cannot mistake an unmarked row for a cleared one. No bytes, role, scope or revision change is required; the edition's identity content for these rows is already correct.

expectedDownstreamEffect: The Colorado JDF family moves from an unstated commercial-use question to a recorded, fail-closed licence determination with a named remedy. The dependency edge into the Edition 1.3 publication gate clears with a licence disposition attached. No Colorado track becomes generatable — the family now carries an explicit distribution blocker in addition to its existing identity, mapping and materialization blockers. The AUTH-02 remap child remains for Session A to create. No packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
